transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-09-14 15:00 PDT
Duration: 43 minutes (scheduled)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (Redwood Product), Tom Reynolds (Polaris Head of Data), Sara Nguyen (Polaris Platform Eng), Luis Ortega (Polaris CFO)

Summary:
Quick console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating Dedicated vs Hosted for storefront personalization and order routing; major concerns are predictable unit economics, latency to store locations, and SOC 2 / encryption. Agreed to run token-level cost model and a staging benchmark.

Topics:
- Console usage analytics and per-route breakdowns
- Token-level cost attribution and model routing policies
- Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs for latency + cost
- Security/compliance: SOC 2, KMS, audit logs, SSO
- Next steps and pricing follow-up

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. Jordan and Priya are with me; Jordan's going to walk through the console and the per-route dashboards.
[00:08] Tom Reynolds (Polaris): Hey Maya, thanks. We got Luis and Sara here too. We built a quick agenda around usage analytics and cost - Alex in ops couldn't make it.
[00:14] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Cool - I'll share my screen in a sec. Quick qualification: are you currently sending requests at storefront-level granularity or aggregated?
[00:22] Sara Nguyen (Polaris): Right now we have per-region endpoints aggregated by store cluster. We don't have per-route telemetry today, which is why we're excited about the console.
[00:29] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Got it. I'll show how per-route dashboards break down tokens, latency, error rates, and cost allocation. Also how routing policies can send lower-latency requests to Dedicated capacity for critical flows.
[02:05] Jordan Lee (Redwood): (screen) This is the Usage Overview - you can see total tokens across models, embeddings, chat usage. Top-right has filters for time-range and model family. Notice the per-route card here, expands into a per-route timeline.
[03:01] Tom Reynolds (Polaris): That per-route cost column - is that real-time or near real-time? We need close to near real-time for day-of flash sales.
[03:09] Jordan Lee (Redwood): It's near real-time, usually a 30-90s lag depending on ingestion. For high-throughput customers we can tune ingestion to be faster; there's a tradeoff with cost and retention.
[04:12] Sara Nguyen (Polaris): The token attribution - how do you handle caching? We prefix cache a lot for product detail prompts.
[04:20] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Good question. We show both raw tokens and billable tokens after applying prefix/KV cache. The console labels cached hits so you can see the delta; sometimes folks see a 25-60% reduction in billable tokens for product-detail flows.
[05:45] Priya Desai (Redwood): Also note the Optimize recommendations - it will suggest batching and a quantization profile per route if you want to lower unit costs for lower-sensitivity flows.
[06:10] Tom Reynolds (Polaris): For our cart-abandonment flows we need sub-200ms p95 for the region - can Redwood hit that on hosted?
[06:22] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Hosted can be fast but it's multi-tenant; typical p95 for similar workloads is around 150-300ms depending on model and prompt size. For strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated pinned capacity in the region - that gives predictable latency and you can allocate GPU pools to the route.
[07:03] Luis Ortega (Polaris): Predictable is key - our finance team wants to avoid token bill shock. How do you show cost per route so we can hold teams accountable?
[07:13] Maya Chen (Redwood): The per-route dashboards include token usage, billable tokens, model mix, and a computed cost column based on your pricing tier or a custom pricing import. You can export CSVs for chargeback.
[08:30] Tom Reynolds (Polaris): Any way to attribute tokens to feature flags or users?
[08:37] Jordan Lee (Redwood): We support tags and metadata on requests - route tags, user-id hash - and the console lets you slice by those. It's not a perfect join if your app doesn't send consistent tags, but when in place it's pretty accurate.
[09:55] Sara Nguyen (Polaris): On security: we need SOC 2, audit logs, and KMS integration. Also SSO via SAML and RBAC so only product owners can see cost dashboards.
[10:07] Maya Chen (Redwood): Absolutely - we'll share our SOC 2 report and the security pack. We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and KMS integration for Dedicated. Console has RBAC and per-role visibility controls.
[11:20] Jordan Lee (Redwood): (narration) back to the console - here's a per-route timeline showing model switch events; you can see a canary rollout where traffic split 10/90 and the cost/latency delta immediately.
[12:40] Tom Reynolds (Polaris): How granular is the cost calc? We have custom pricing for some models; can we input internal cost multipliers?
[12:50] Priya Desai (Redwood): Yes - you can plug in custom cost profiles per model and apply multipliers per team or SKU. That feeds the route cost column and the chargeback exports.
[14:15] Luis Ortega (Polaris): If we go Dedicated, do we still get the console analytics? And is the billing line-item separated from Hosted usage?
[14:25] Maya Chen (Redwood): Dedicated includes the same console analytics and dashboards - billing will show Reserved vs On-demand and you can tag by project. Dedicated reserved capacity shows separate cost buckets and you can map them to internal GL codes.
[15:10] Tom Reynolds (Polaris): Can the console show ROI or cost-per-successful-recommendation? We do A/B on recommendations.
[15:25] Jordan Lee (Redwood): You can import custom success metrics or tag requests and then compute derived metrics in the console. We also integrate with your event sink so you can join inference events with conversion events. That's how teams measure cost per conversion.
[17:05] Sara Nguyen (Polaris): On compliance, the audit logs - how long retained? We need 12 months for audits.
[17:12] Maya Chen (Redwood): Audit logs retention depends on plan; Dedicated and Private can have extended retention. We also offer an add-on for long-term log archives (S3) for 12+ months.
[18:00] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Switching to cost breakdown examples - here's a sample customer: route A used 1.2M billable tokens last month, model mix 60% gpt-like-open, 40% small open model. Cost calc shows $Xk but optimized suggestions cut it to $Yk by changing model mix and enabling prefix cache.
[19:45] Tom Reynolds (Polaris): That heuristic for suggesting model swaps - is it automated rollouts or just recommendations? We worry about quality regressions.
[19:55] Priya Desai (Redwood): Right now Optimize gives recommended model/quantization profiles and simulated cost/quality impact; you can run evals on your prompt sets. For production we support staged rollouts with automatic fallback if quality dips. So manual approval required to commit a swap across prod.
[22:05] Luis Ortega (Polaris): For finance signoff, can you provide an example SOW with committed throughput and SLAs?
[22:12] Maya Chen (Redwood): Yes - we'll include a draft SOW with Dedicated reserved size, p95 SLOs, and uptime SLA; we can also include a consumption example with cost per million tokens.
[24:00] Tom Reynolds (Polaris): On the token-level cost model, can you include different prompt templates? We have variable prompt lengths by template.
[24:12] Jordan Lee (Redwood): We can - Jordan: I'll model token distributions per template if you share a CSV with sample prompts and traffic weights. That will give you a per-route and per-template estimated monthly spend.
[25:30] Sara Nguyen (Polaris): For latency, region routing - can Redwood route to nearest Dedicated pod in eu-west vs us-west? We have stores in both.
[25:40] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Yes, smart routing supports region-based routing policies; you can also set cost-based fallbacks to a cheaper region if latency SLO still met. For ultimate control, Private deployments let you host inference on-prem in a region.
[27:00] Tom Reynolds (Polaris): We might need on-prem for some PII flows. What's the difference in console features on Private?
[27:10] Maya Chen (Redwood): Private has the same console UX; audit logs and RBAC are controlled by your infra. There are differences in data egress and where logs are stored. We'll include a comparison doc.
[29:30] Luis Ortega (Polaris): One more on chargeback: can teams be restricted from switching models without approvals to avoid cost spikes?
[29:40] Priya Desai (Redwood): Yes - RBAC + guardrails: you can require approvals for model changes, limit allowed models per route, and set budget caps per team. Console will trigger alerts on budget thresholds.
[31:15] Tom Reynolds (Polaris): Any known gotchas with prefix caching and personalization? We do dynamic personalization tokens inside templates.
[31:25] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Personalization with cache requires careful tokenization - you should separate static vs dynamic sections and use hashed identifiers for user-specific tokens. We can consult on prompt engineering in the PoC.
[33:05] Sara Nguyen (Polaris): For the perf benchmark - we want to measure p95 for their largest prompt set with KV cache warm and cold. Is that straightforward?
[33:15] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Totally - typical benchmark includes cold start, warm cache, and steady-state. We'll script replay of sample traffic against a staging Dedicated pool. Expect to see variance on cold starts, then stable p95 after cache warmed.
[35:00] Tom Reynolds (Polaris): Pricing question: do you include a margin on top of GPU cost in Dedicated? Our procurement wants unit economics transparent.
[35:10] Maya Chen (Redwood): We provide a pricing breakdown - reserved capacity is a flat commit + per-token for overage. We'll show model-level unit economics and the margin. Jordan will include a cost model example.
[36:40] Luis Ortega (Polaris): If we do a hybrid (Hosted for non-critical flows, Dedicated for mission-critical), is routing config managed in console?
[36:50] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Yes - routing policies are configurable per route in the console; you can set weight-based splits, latency-first, or cost-first policies, and automatic fallback rules.
[38:10] Priya Desai (Redwood): Quick demo of the next-steps panel - on the console you can create a playbook for rollout: add canary percentages, alert thresholds, and automatic rollback on quality regression.
[39:25] Tom Reynolds (Polaris): OK that helps. Let's recap next steps.
[39:33] Maya Chen (Redwood): Recap: I'll send pricing + SOW and the SOC 2/security pack. Jordan will run the token-level cost model once Sara shares sample prompts/weights. We'll schedule a 2-hour staging perf benchmark (Jordan + Sara).
[39:52] Tom Reynolds (Polaris): Timeline-wise we want a pilot by mid-October; does that fit?
[40:00] Maya Chen (Redwood): Mid-October pilot is doable - we'll align on scope in the SOW.
[40:12] Luis Ortega (Polaris): I'll want an itemized cost plus reserved commit options for finance.
[40:18] Maya Chen (Redwood): Got it - included in the SOW.
[41:05] Sara Nguyen (Polaris): I'll upload sample prompts and traffic weights after the call.
[41:10] Jordan Lee (Redwood): Great - once we have that I'll run the model and share the spreadsheet.
[42:00] Maya Chen (Redwood): Thanks everyone - we'll follow up.
[42:10] Meeting end
